chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the spending of dirhams that are predominantly silver, he said: 'If the dominant substance upon them is silver, then there is no harm in spending them.'

key_terms.الْمَحْمُولِ عَلَيْهَا: Predominantly / Carried upon it (referring to the dominant substance)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on spending dirhams that contain a mixture of metals?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding mixed currency, establishing the principle of *ghalib* (predominance) to determine the legal status of assets. This criterion allows for the permissibility of spending dirhams with mixed metal content provided silver constitutes the majority, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Islamic period. It underscores the Shia legal methodology of prioritizing the dominant characteristic when resolving ambiguity in commercial transactions.
